## AI Industry

OpenAI’s infrastructure expansion onto Google Cloud marks a strategic shift away from exclusive Azure dependency, reducing friction for enterprise multi-cloud architectures.

- [OpenAI partners with Google Cloud to offer AI models, codex workflows](https://news.google.?oc=5): OpenAI is broadening availability of its models and workflows natively within Google Cloud. For IT post-merger integrations, this significantly diminishes cloud-lock-in risk; acquirers running native GCP environments no longer face forced Azure re-platforming or brittle third-party API wrappers to ingest standard OpenAI capabilities.
- [Chinese AI Powers Half of Korea's New Models: Study](https://news.google.?oc=5): A new industry study found that roughly 50% of new South Korean AI models rely on Chinese foundational architectures (such as Alibaba’s Qwen). This introduces major supply chain and regulatory red flags for cross-border software M&A diligence, where targets claiming "in-house" AI may carry hidden exposure to Chinese open-source licenses, export controls, and foreign data-governance scrutiny.
- [Why Anthropic’s draft bill sets $1 billion threshold for AI risk](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiigFBVV95cUxNWWhaN0lXMkdTcldqYTBoVktsbUx1QzI3emNYTmZ2Q2ZENEp0NFh2My1VeGZLbnlYbS1SMFNkak1FLXk1eGtaMUMtME9EOFpCV3N4TG45ZEUyNHRiVFNZcHFSTURZel9kSzNKRU8ySHBNZmtrcEg0VkNrdHhjUF8yWFVjMEFlYzhpcVE?oc=5): Anthropic is floating model legislation that establishes mandatory safety and reporting rules only for models exceeding $1 billion in compute costs. If adopted as an industry benchmark, it shields application-layer and mid-market AI targets from immediate statutory compliance drag, insulating tuck-in acquisitions from frontier-tier regulatory liabilities.
